description: One block that one application reached, with the acres covered on it and — where the machine carries two sets — which set was running there. A tank that went out over four blocks is four of these rows and four Spray REI records, because the acres differ per block and the restriction is a fact about a place. The REI record this row opened is linked back so the application and the restriction are one chain rather than two registers somebody has to join by hand.

fields.description: 'Field' for a planted block, 'Asset Register' for a block-shaped asset tag — the same pair Spray REI and Farm Task use, so a restriction, a task and an application on one block all key alike.
fields.label: Block DocType

fields.description: Acres actually covered on this block. Per block rather than one figure for the pass, because product used is rate times acres and a four-block pass has four answers.
fields.label: Acres

fields.description: Which nozzle set was running on THIS block. 'A then B' is the flip actually performed mid-block. Recorded per block because the flip usually happens at a block edge, and an application that says 'we flipped somewhere' cannot tell anybody which block got which product.
fields.label: Nozzle Set Used
fields.options:
Both
A
B
A then B
B then A

fields.description: The restricted-entry window this block's application opened. Written back after the REI record is created, so the application and the restriction are one chain.
fields.label: REI Record

fields.description: When this block was started, where the pass was long enough for the blocks to differ. Left blank the application's own start is used.
fields.label: Started At

fields.description: When this block FINISHED. The restricted-entry window for this block runs from here where it is set, and from the application's completion where it is not — a block sprayed at eight in the morning does not stay shut because the last block of the pass finished at two.
fields.label: Completed At

name: Spray Application Block
